name: Data-Processing Invariance

title: Proof
body_md: Relative entropy belongs to the family of Csisz\'ar $f$-divergences with convex generator $f(t) = t \ln t$. By the monotonicity theorem for $f$-divergences under sub-$\sigma$-algebras \citep{csiszar1967information, cover2006elements}, measurable transformations can only preserve or contract information. Setting the input space as $\mathcal{M}_1(\mathcal{Z})$ and output space as $\Theta$ under the Borel-measurable mapping $\mathcal{A}$ establishes the inequality. The complete measure-theoretic proof is provided in Appendix~\ref{sec:proof-dpi}.

head: environment
name: Analytical Partition Divergence

title: Remark
body_md: While the relative entropy between two finite-dimensional Dirichlet distributions is a known identity in exponential family statistics, our key insight is recognizing that under the Data Processing Inequality, the infinite-dimensional non-parametric divergence between the DP posterior and prior contracts onto this closed-form partition statistic over $\mathcal{P}$. This completely replaces the classical dimension-dependent Gaussian divergence with an exact, analytical finite-sample certificate.
